phase2.verdict: The eligibleAmount settlement basis is proven live on v5: three identical notes settled at one price paid 60/30/0 exactly proportional to the stock the owner still held at each settle moment, with every reserve releasing in full and the vault solvent at every step. Deployed v4 would have paid 60/60/60 — this is behavioral proof that commit 569ef97 changed settlement, not just tests.

verification: All four v5 protocol contracts source-verified on the explorer 2026-09-16 (AssetRegistry, ProtectionOracle, SherwoodVault, ProtectionNote — solc 0.8.35, optimizer 200 runs, constructor args included for the oracle (sequencerUptimeFeed=0, gracePeriod=3600), the vault (MockUSDG, 2000 bps) and the note (registry, oracle, vault); the registry has none). Submitted with forge verify-contract against the explorer's Etherscan-compatible API (accepts a keyless dummy key); every constructor-args blob was byte-validated against the tail of its on-chain creation transaction before submission, and each verify returned 'Pass - Verified'.
notes: v5 deployed 2026-09-14. It carries everything v4 lacked: the Chainlink L2 sequencer-uptime gate (off here by design — 46630 publishes no feed), the 8-decimal feed scale check at registration and rotation, the tightened withdrawSurplus/setBufferBps rules that can never breach invariant 1, and the eligibleAmount settlement basis (payout computed on min(note.amount, stock the owner still holds), reserve always released in full; commit 569ef97, 164/164 tests green). The oracle gained constructor arguments, so this had to be a fresh deploy, not a config nudge.

v4 is abandoned but not deleted: its four contracts stay on-chain with their history, and the demoNotes entries below were executed against the v4 stack (their tx hashes reference v4 addresses 0x70A97604.../0x2725cC6c...). Both v4 demo legs were settled and receipt-verified on 2026-09-14 before the redeploy — payout leg tx 0x79c3366e..., zero-payout leg tx 0x42b9c263... — so the evidence trail lives entirely on one version, which was the point of waiting.

v5 next steps, in order: fund the vault (faucet claim + vault.deposit, the v5 vault holds nothing yet), then run the demo create/settle path against the v5 addresses. DemoSettle now demands DEMO_SETTLE_PRICE explicitly (commit 6340b13) instead of defaulting to $100 — the default would have paid note 2 $5 and destroyed its zero-payout boundary.

v4 redeployed for one reason: SherwoodVault.token is immutable, so the v3 vault will forever point at official testnet USDG, a token no protocol wallet has ever received. v3/v2/v1 are abandoned with zero funds and superseded.

Position guard is unchanged in v4 and v5 (create() reverts InsufficientPosition unless the caller holds the protected stock); proven on-chain in the v3 simulation on 2026-09-12 and covered by tests since.

Frontend is repointed at this stack: v4 addresses and MockUSDG are the built-in defaults in frontend/lib/addresses.ts (mirrored in the gitignored frontend/.env.local), and `npm run build` was verified with no env file present, so a Vercel deploy needs no configuration.

Demo write path executed 2026-09-13 on v4: script/DemoCreate.s.sol funded the vault with 50 MockUSDG and bought note 1 (0.1 TSLA, $250 entry, 80%, 1 day) entirely in MockUSDG, paid from the 1,000 claimed from its faucet. Both notes settled 2026-09-14 — see each demoNote's settlement object.

Deploy note for this chain: forge script needs --private-key passed explicitly for --broadcast; relying on the PRIVATE_KEY env var alone left the broadcast using Foundry's default sender and nothing was signed (the first v4 attempt produced zero deployed code). Dry runs need --sender set to the deployer too, or the DemoFeed's onlyOwner check reverts NotOwner. Expect an EIP-3855/PUSH0 warning for chain 46630 — v1 through v5 all deployed and execute fine. On this device run long broadcasts under termux-wake-lock; an unattended v4-era broadcast slept mid-run and submitted nothing.
